findings.current: “At the very least, I’m pretty sure it wasn’t something like, ‘Is our son eating well?’”
findings.defect: “Our son” implies a shared parent; the imagined letter is from Sima Gong about his own son.
findings.rationale: 우리 아들 is a familiar Korean way for a parent to say “my son” here.
findings.replacement: “At the very least, I’m pretty sure it wasn’t something like, ‘Is my son eating well?’”
findings.source: 최소한 우리 아들 밥은 잘 먹고 다니냐, 뭐 그런 내용은 아니라는 것 정도.

findings.current: “Is that any way to talk? Even that Taishan fellow—or was it Gangsan?—would know better.”
findings.defect: “Would know better” makes Taishan’s judgment of Taekyung’s manners the point. Jeok means even Taishan could work out the obvious fact Taekyung just stated.
findings.rationale: 그건 알겠다 refers back to Taekyung’s guess about what the letter did not say.
findings.replacement: “You call that an answer? Even that Taishan—or Gangsan, whatever his name is—could tell you that.”
findings.source: 그건 태산인가 강산인가 하는 그놈도 알겠다.

findings.current: “You’ve come a long way. You really have.”
findings.defect: The English suggests admiration for Sima Gong’s progress rather than Jeok’s contempt at his audacity.
findings.rationale: Jeok spits before saying this in response to the suspected secret letter; 많이 컸군 is pointed and disparaging in context.

findings.current: “He was secretly burning a letter all alone, where no one could see him.”
findings.defect: “Where no one could see him” changes secrecy into a claim about physical visibility, and “letter” drops the explicit secret-letter designation.
findings.rationale: 아무도 모르게 means without anyone knowing; 밀서 is a secret letter.
findings.replacement: “He was burning a secret letter alone, without anyone knowing.”
findings.source: 아무도 모르게 홀로 밀서(密書)를 태우고 있었다라.

findings.current: He’d still been putting away five meals a day. How was that eating less?
findings.defect: The neutral “putting away” softens Taekyung’s crude description of Taishan eating.
findings.rationale: 처먹었는데 is deliberately coarse, sharpening the joke about Taishan’s supposed loss of appetite.
findings.replacement: He was still stuffing his face five times a day. How was that eating less?
findings.source: 그 와중에도 꾸준히 하루 다섯 끼를 처먹었는데 그게 어떻게 깨작깨작인가.

findings.current:
Why did it feel like I could see the Korean flag waving before my eyes?

A classic movie I’d seen long ago came to mind—but only for a moment.
findings.defect: The literal flag image leaves the film-title allusion inaccessible to readers who do not know its Korean title.
findings.rationale: 태극기 names both the flag and the film evoked by the following sentence; a brief note preserves the image and explains the connection without changing the prose.
findings.replacement:
Why did it feel like I could see the Korean flag waving before my eyes?[^1]

A classic movie I’d seen long ago came to mind—but only for a moment.

[^1]: *Taegukgi* (“Korean flag”) is the Korean title of a film about brothers caught up in the Korean War.
findings.source:
마치 눈앞에서 태극기가 펄럭이는 듯한 이 기분은 뭘까.

오래전에 봤던 고전 명작 영화가 문득 떠올랐지만, 그것도 잠시뿐이었다.

summary: The draft preserves the scene’s main events but alters several implications in dialogue and misses one useful cultural reference.
